from: the Rev D slim tag (BaggageClaims_Tag_RevD_Engineering.md and _Design.md in Files)
about: The Rev D slim leather-look tag the owner approved on 22 Nov 2026 at 19:00 ("yes this is perfect, a perfect design"): direction A Heritage, colourway A1 Saddle, one CR2032 with a 1 F supercapacitor, an nRF52832 on a custom board. The 2 x AA design's parts and wires are retired only while they still read as seeded; requirements and tests tied to two AA cells are brought to Rev D's figures, each an estimate where it is one. Every row names the Rev D document and section it comes from.

rows.sourceLocation: section 1, what you are choosing; section 4, direction A
rows.title: Which enclosure design ships?
rows.body: Rev D, the slim leather-look tag, offered in three directions and two colourways each, every one 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm with the same inside and passing the same 20 of 20 checks of its own generator. Chosen: direction A, Heritage (square shoulders cut at 45 degrees, saddle stitching in the thread colour, a blind-stamped oval maker's mark, a perforated panel across the top), colourway A1, Saddle: Bambu Lab PETG HF Peanut Brown body, Bambu Lab PETG HF Cream thread and lettering, Bambu Lab TPU for AMS Black strap. Renders, the assembly and the two print plates are in Files, folder Design and build.

rows.sourceLocation: section 0, summary; section 5, mechanical consequences
rows.title: Which form factor ships?
rows.body: A slim leather-look luggage tag, 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm, about 62 to 64 g with the tracker (estimate), hanging about 10 mm under the handle on a TPU strap, with a pocket for an AirTag-style tracker behind a bayonet door and a name card in the back. It replaces the 80 x 60 x 42 mm box and the 2 x AA design (Rev B, and Rev C's box): about a third of the box's volume and 30 % of its thickness. The tracker's 8.0 mm sets the thickness.

options.label: 80 x 60 x 42 mm box on two AA cells (Rev B, Rev C)
options.outcome: About 80 dB at 1 m and about 6 months on a pair of cells; a large object dangling from the handle.

options.label: Slim tag, 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm, on one CR2032 (Rev D)
options.outcome: About 70 dB at 1 m and about 9 months on a cell (estimates); a custom circuit board replaces the breakout boards.

data.source: Rev D engineering, sections 0 and 5; Rev D design, section 2

rows.ruling: Owner, 22 Nov 2026, in his direction for Rev D: "more like a leather-looking, high-quality baggage tag ... change the double-A batteries to a watch battery to make it smaller ... We cannot have a large dangling object. It must have a pocket to fit an AirTag and be a little larger"; and at 19:00, of the Rev D tag: "yes this is perfect, a perfect design".

rows.sourceLocation: section 1, name and tagline
rows.title: Which lines go on the tag?
rows.body: As rendered and approved with the design: on the front, BAGGAGE CLAIMS / MK1 in the stamp and the tagline "Your luggage finally talks back." (the launch video script's line under the title card, 0:06); on the tracker door in the back, "FRAGILE — and emotionally unstable." (the owner's line, word for word). Lettering Montserrat Bold, an open-licence placeholder until a brand kit exists. No third-party name or logo anywhere.

options.outcome: As on the Rev D renders.

rows.sourceLocation: section 1, airline rules; section 2.1, options compared
rows.title: Which cell powers the tag?
rows.body: One CR2032 lithium coin cell with a 1 F, 2.7 V supercapacitor that carries the speaker's bursts: the cell never drives the speaker; it refills the capacitor at up to 2.6 mA through 470 ohm, inside its 3 mA continuous rating, and the capacitor gives the 1 W peaks through a boost converter. 0.07 g of lithium metal, under the 0.3 g under which a device may stay on in checked baggage. No port, no charger; the user changes one CR2032 about every nine months (estimate).

options.label: Two AA alkaline cells, 3.3 V boost (Rev B)
options.outcome: Not lithium; needs a 2 x 46 mm battery bay and the 20 mm deep speaker: the box.

options.label: One CR2032 straight to the amplifier
options.outcome: About 53 dB at 1 m: inaudible in a terminal.

options.label: One CR2032 and a 1 F supercapacitor buffer
options.outcome: About 70 dB at 1 m, about 9 months (estimates); 0.07 g lithium.

options.label: One CR2450 and the same buffer
options.outcome: About 26 months, about 0.19 g lithium (estimate); the 24.5 mm cell does not fit beside the speaker without a wider tag.

options.label: LIR2450 rechargeable and USB-C
options.outcome: 0.43 Wh; a charging port in the face, a charger and a protection chip, and no louder.

options.label: Flat 150 mAh LiPo and USB-C
options.outcome: 0.56 Wh; a pouch cell in a bag that is thrown and crushed.

data.note: The airline rules, as read on 22 Nov 2026 (Rev D engineering, section 1). IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, 66th edition, Table 2.3.A (https://www.iata.org/contentassets/6fea26dd84d24b26a7a1fd5788561d6e/dgr-66-en-2.3.a.pdf): baggage with installed lithium batteries may go as checked baggage only if the batteries "contain no more than 0.3 g lithium metal or for lithium ion must not exceed 2.7 Wh"; portable electronic devices: "Devices in checked baggage must be completely switched off and must be protected from damage". IATA Guidance Document for Passengers Travelling with Lithium Batteries 2026 (https://www.iata.org/contentassets/6fea26dd84d24b26a7a1fd5788561d6e/passengers_travelling_with_lithium_batteries.pdf): in checked baggage "the device must be completely switched off (not in sleep or hibernation mode)", with a footnote exempting devices of 0.3 g or less of lithium metal, or 2.7 Wh or less. FAA PackSafe, Baggage Equipped with Lithium Batteries (https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/baggage-with-lithium-batteries): "lithium content not exceeding 0.3 grams" or "a Watt-hour rating not exceeding 2.7 Wh"; "If you choose to equip a checked bag with a baggage tracking device, then it must meet the size limits above"; "Check with the airline before traveling with these devices". FAA PackSafe, Portable Electronic Devices Containing Batteries (https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/portable-electronic-devices-with-batteries): devices in checked bags "must be completely powered off and protected to prevent unintentional activation or damage"; spare lithium batteries "are always prohibited in checked baggage". FAA PackSafe, Lithium Batteries (https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/lithium-batteries): lithium metal "limited to 2 grams of lithium content per battery". The CR2032's 0.07 g: the Duracell CR2032 sheet (https://www.duracell.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/CR2032CH_225mAh.pdf). The IATA documents were read through a web reader. Still to watch: airlines may set stricter rules, and no rule names a device that talks.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Custom circuit board, 24 x 35 mm
rows.body: Two layers, 0.8 mm FR-4, ENIG (pads for the cell springs), corners R 1.5. It carries everything but the speaker, the supercapacitor and the tracker: U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, Q1, Q2, R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, C1, C2, PAS, Y1, L1, L3, S1, S2, BT1, and the programming pads J1 (a Tag-Connect TC2030 footprint, no part fitted). Components on the back side up to 1.2 mm high, the two cell springs on the front side, both switches on its right-hand edge. Clamped between four printed posts and four pads on the back plate. Price per board of a 5-board prototype order; it needs a design and a layout first (about $20 for the first five plus a stencil, estimate). Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

geometry.basisSource: 24 x 35 x 0.8 mm: the Rev D design (engineering, section 4)

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Board assembly
rows.body: Stencil and reflow by hand at one to five boards (own labour not costed, so $0), turnkey assembly at a hundred. 0.4 mm-pitch parts: not perfboard work. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

data.source: Own bench; an assembly house at 100

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Controller chip, nRF52832
rows.body: nRF52832-QFAA, QFN-48 6 x 6 mm, run from the cell directly; its radio is never started and no antenna is fitted. 512 kB flash of its own; the clips are in U3. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Crystals Y1 and Y2, 32 MHz and 32.768 kHz
rows.body: 2016 and 2012 packages, for U1. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: DC/DC inductors L1 and L2, 10 uH and 15 nH
rows.body: For U1's own DC/DC converter. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Motion sensor chip, LSM6DSO class
rows.body: 6-axis accelerometer and gyro, LGA-14 2.5 x 3 x 0.83 mm, +/-16 g and +/-2000 degrees a second, FIFO and wake-up interrupt, on SPI. Replaces the Adafruit MPU-6050 breakout, which is a third of the tag's inside and draws more than a coin cell gives with its gyro on. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Clip flash, 8 MB SPI NOR
rows.body: MX25R6435F class, wide supply: about 245 s of 16 kHz PCM or about 980 s as 4-bit ADPCM (calculated). Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Amplifier chip, MAX98357A
rows.body: The I2S class-D amplifier of the 2 x AA design as a chip (TQFN-16 3 x 3) on the board; fed from the boosted 3.3 V only while a clip plays. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Boost converter, 3.3 V, TPS61023 class
rows.body: Starts from 0.5 V, switch of 3 A or more (recalled), 3.3 V out; raises the supercapacitor for the amplifier and is enabled only for a clip. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Boost inductor, 1 uH 3 A
rows.body: 2520 package, for U5. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Reverse-cell P-MOSFET
rows.body: SOT-23, in the cell's lead after the off switch, gate to ground: a cell fitted the wrong way does no harm. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Charge switch P-MOSFET
rows.body: SOT-23, switched by the controller (CHG_EN): it lets the cell refill the supercapacitor through R1 and stops at 2.6 V. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Charge resistor, 470 ohm
rows.body: From the charge switch to the supercapacitor: 2.6 mA at 1.8 V on the capacitor, 0.85 mA at 2.6 V (calculated), inside the CR2032's 3 mA continuous. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Capacitor sense resistor, upper
rows.body: Divider from the supercapacitor to the controller's ADC (V_SC). Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Capacitor sense resistor, lower
rows.body: Lower half of the V_SC divider, to ground. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Cell sense resistor, upper
rows.body: Divider from the cell rail to the controller's ADC (V_CELL), read under the 2 mA charge load so a tired cell shows. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Cell sense resistor, lower
rows.body: Lower half of the V_CELL divider, to ground. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Boost enable pull-down
rows.body: Holds the boost converter off while the controller is unpowered or asleep, so a charged capacitor cannot drive the amplifier with the off switch off. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Cell rail capacitor, 100 uF
rows.body: Carries the controller's bursts (about 10 mA for milliseconds) off the cell. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Cell rail capacitor, 10 uF
rows.body: Beside C1 at the controller. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Other passives
rows.body: Decoupling and the DC/DC parts, about eight: the rest of the Rev D note's passives line ($0.80, $0.80 and $0.20 in all with R1 to R6, C1 and C2). Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Supercapacitor 1 F, 2.7 V
rows.body: Eaton HV0810-2R7105-R: 1 F, 2.7 V, 0.2 ohm, 10 uA leakage, 8.5 x 13.5 mm (the maker's page, read 22 Nov 2026). Between 2.6 and 1.8 V it holds 1.76 J, about 2.5 clips at full level (calculated). Lies in two printed saddles beside the tracker, leads through a notch to the board. Price: an estimate.

geometry.basisSource: 8.5 x 13.5 mm: the maker's page (Eaton HV0810-2R7105-R), read 22 Nov 2026

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Speaker 28 mm, 4 ohm, 3 W
rows.body: PUI Audio AS02804PR-N50-R: 28 mm, 7.5 mm seated, 4 ohm, 3 W, 76.5 dBA at 3 W and 1 m, $7.33 one, $4.38 a hundred (DigiKey, read 22 Nov 2026). About 70 dB at 1 m at full level in the tag (estimate). On a 0.5 mm foam gasket under the perforated panel, three printed fingers hold it, in a sealed 5.6 cm3 chamber.

geometry.basisSource: 28 mm diameter, 7.5 mm seated: the reseller's page (DigiKey), read 22 Nov 2026

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Off switch, side-actuated slide
rows.body: SPDT slide switch on the board's right-hand edge (C&K PCM12 class), in the cell's lead before everything: off, the cell is disconnected. Its lever sits 0.5 mm under the edge surface in a slot, so a knock cannot move it. Price: an estimate.

data.search: C&K PCM12 right angle slide switch

geometry.basisSource: Typical of the C&K PCM12 class (Rev D engineering, section 4), unverified

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Mode button, side-actuated tactile
rows.body: 3.5 x 2.9 mm side-actuated tactile switch (SKRT class) on the board's right-hand edge, plunger 0.5 mm under the edge surface: tap for volume, hold for the voice pack, 10 s to reset. Price: an estimate.

geometry.basisSource: Typical of the SKRT class (Rev D engineering, section 4), unverified

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Cell contacts, rim and centre springs
rows.body: Two springs soldered to the board's front side press the cell onto its door: the rim spring is +, the centre spring -. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Coin cell CR2032
rows.body: One CR2032 lithium coin cell, 20.0 x 3.2 mm (Murata), 0.07 g of lithium metal (Duracell's sheet, read 22 Nov 2026): under the 0.3 g under which a device may stay on in checked baggage. In a printed cup under a bayonet coin door in the front. About 9 months at four travel days a month (estimate). Price: an estimate.

geometry.basisSource: 20.0 x 3.2 mm: the Murata CR2032 data sheet, read 22 Nov 2026

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Speaker gasket and chamber foam
rows.body: Gasket ring 28 OD / 23 ID in 0.5 mm closed-cell foam, and foam tape for the chamber's seal. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

data.search: 0.5 mm closed cell foam sheet adhesive

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.title: Tracker, AirTag-style (the buyer's own)
rows.body: Not part of the product and not costed: the buyer drops their own tracker (31.9 mm across, 8.0 mm thick, domed both sides) into the pocket behind the bayonet door in the back. One is needed to try the pocket on the prototype. It is its own device with its own cell, which does not count against the tag's lithium.

geometry.basisSource: 31.9 x 8.0 mm: the owner's brief; the domed profile is assumed

rows.sourceLocation: section 10, printing and estimates
rows.title: Tag body, printed (PETG, two colours)
rows.body: Direction A Heritage, colourway A1 Saddle: Bambu Lab PETG HF Peanut Brown with the stitches, the stamp's rules and the lettering inlaid 0.6 mm in Bambu Lab PETG HF Cream. 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm outside; rim 3.0 mm, front skin 1.6 mm with the perforated panel (61 holes through over the speaker) and the coin-cell cup; pebble grain modelled into the face. Printed front down in job 1. Estimate, not sliced: 25.4 g of PETG in the body and its front inlay, plus 3.2 g of purge for the job's eight colour changes, at $20 a kg: $0.57.

geometry.basisSource: 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm: the Rev D design (section 2) and its own size check

rows.sourceLocation: section 10, printing and estimates
rows.title: Back plate, printed (PETG)
rows.body: Drops into the body's rim and is held by eight printed snap hooks; carries the name-card pocket (50 x 32 card under 1.5 mm lips) and the tracker door's seat; stitching inlaid in cream. Estimate, not sliced: 6.2 g of PETG at $20 a kg: $0.12.

rows.sourceLocation: section 10, printing and estimates
rows.title: Tracker door, printed (PETG)
rows.body: Bayonet door in the back plate (opening 32.9 mm), turned 60 degrees with a coin; carries "FRAGILE — and emotionally unstable." inlaid in cream. Estimate, not sliced: 1.9 g of PETG at $20 a kg: $0.04.

rows.sourceLocation: section 10, printing and estimates
rows.title: Coin-cell door, printed (PETG)
rows.body: Bayonet door in the front (opening 20.8 mm) over the CR2032, its perforations continuing the panel's lattice. Estimate, not sliced: 0.7 g of PETG at $20 a kg: $0.01.

rows.sourceLocation: section 10, printing and estimates
rows.title: Strap, printed (TPU)
rows.body: 14 x 2.0 mm TPU strap in Bambu Lab TPU for AMS Black, through the 18 x 3.2 mm slot, round the handle, a stud pressed through a hole; it holds the tag about 10 mm under the handle. Printed in job 2. Estimate, not sliced: 6.3 g of TPU at $40 a kg (a round figure): $0.25.

geometry.basisSource: 14 x 2.0 mm strap (the Rev D design, check 16); its loop above the slot drawn straight, 40 mm

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.6, bill of materials
rows.appendBody: Rev D (the slim tag, 22 Nov 2026): the electronics come to $29.02 for one unit, $27.02 a unit for five and $16.68 a unit for a hundred (estimates), and the printed parts to about $0.99 of filament (estimate, not sliced); the tracker is the buyer's own and not counted.
